quotes.text: Every great journey begins the same way: plant your feet and choose a direction. Today, you chose.
Back day is my favorite day. I can't see my back, so I'm assuming it's incredible.
Fire is the element of power, but power without breath burns out. Breathe first, then push.
(Momo's thoughts) Stretching. Stretching. Is that a melon? No. More stretching.
Leg day? More like why-does-everything-hurt-and-who-moved-the-stairs day.
Water is the most adaptable element. Change the plan when you need to, but never the goal.
Chest day is the only day I'm qualified to give advice. My advice: more chest.
When you let go of what you're carrying, you can finally fly. Rest days are how you let go.
The ground tells me everything. Plant your feet like you mean it and nobody will push you around.
I pulled so hard on that last row, I think I'm related to a polar bear dog now.
I spent years chasing someone else's idea of honor. Real honor is doing the hard work for the right reasons.
Rest day! The best day! Wait, there's foam rolling? A foam roller is just a log that hates me!
I stacked my cabbages into the perfect squat rack. Then the Avatar rolled through. Again.
Precision is a form of respect. Respect the movement and it will respect you back.
I practiced a whole speech about warming up properly. ...Warm up. Properly. Okay, it went better in my head.
The mind must be free before the body can follow. Breathe, and begin.
A mountain is only a pile of small stones that refused to quit. Add one stone today.
Sokka, you do not get bigger biceps by flexing at every puddle you walk past.
Respect the fire. A wild flame destroys; a controlled flame forges.
Appa says rest days are his favorite. Appa says every day is his favorite. Appa mostly says grrrrr.
I can't see your form, Twinkletoes, but I can feel it. It's shaking like a nervous badgermole.
Even the moon has phases. Rest is not falling behind; it is part of the light.
A man needs three things: a good pot of tea, a warm fire, and a spotter who isn't watching the clouds.
Energy flows best through a body that is not knotted with worry. Untie one knot today.
Balance is not something you find. It is something you build, rep by rep, until it holds you.
Life is like a swamp: smelly, mysterious, and somehow great for your forearms.
The heat that tests you is the same heat that tempers you.
The secret to a good mobility session is the same as the secret to a good fruit pie: patience, and no sneaking bites.
A hundred and twelve years old and I have never once skipped leg day. Because I am a MAD GENIUS!
A strong crew pulls together. Your back is the crew that keeps every swing on course.
My aura is pink today! That means push-ups! Okay, my aura means push-ups every day.
Air is freedom, and freedom grows out of discipline, not the other way around.
My father taught me that patience is the strength of stone. It doesn't rush, and it doesn't break.
Pull-ups are a boomerang for your whole body. You go up. You come back. Repeat.
A blade is only as good as the patience that shaped it. You are being shaped.
I can't stretch my legs much, but I can glide right past you while you foam roll. Hi!
The Boulder has a confession. The Boulder skipped leg day once. The Boulder could not climb into the ring.
I have seen many winters, child. Every one of them ended. Keep pulling through yours.
Lateral raises. Wow. Thrilling. I'll try to contain my excitement.
Letting go doesn't mean you stop caring. It means you trust the process enough to breathe.
You don't need to see the bar to lift it. Feel the floor and trust what it tells you.
In my day we did curls with buckets of ice water. Uphill. Both ways. In a blizzard.
Lighting the spark is easy. Keeping the flame alive through winter is the true test.
Foam rolling is like tea: painful when it is too hot, wonderful when you are patient.
My plan: squat heavy, eat meat, repeat. Is it a good plan? It's a plan with meat in it.
Push and pull are the same breath. You can't hit hard if you can't bring your arm back home.
Uncle says my push press looks like an angry turtle-duck. I'm choosing to take that as a compliment.
Rest is not the absence of training. It is training for the spirit.
Roots grow in the dark long before anyone admires the tree. Do the quiet work.
My training philosophy has three pillars: meat, sarcasm and lat pulldowns.
Getting knocked down isn't the end. It's the part of the story where you find out who you are.
I tried yoga once. The downward dog bit me.
You call that a lunge? I've seen cabbages roll downhill with better form!
Water is soft, yet it carves mountains. Gentle, steady effort is the strongest force there is.
I've served under many commanders. None of them skipped shoulder prehab. Well, one did. We don't talk about him.
Patience is a sky without edges. Your progress has all the room it needs to grow.
Strength without control is just noise. Control without strength is just hope. Train both.
When I was young we didn't have face pulls. We had icebergs, and we pulled them.
Energy goes where your attention goes. Pay attention to your shoulders and they'll pay you back.
I invented a machine that does your stretches for you. It exploded. Please do your own stretches.
Rule one of earthbending: never let a staircase know you're afraid of it.
Your form should move like a river: no wasted motion, no hurry, no stopping.
Never underestimate the power of a triceps pushdown, or of the jasmine tea afterward.
To open the air chakra, release grief. To open your hips, release your hurry.
Warriors aren't made on the battlefield. They're made in the thousand practices nobody watches.
I named my left bicep Boomerang. It always comes back to the gym.
Strength used carelessly becomes a debt. Strength used wisely becomes a gift.
I'm a hundred and twelve years old and I still can't touch my toes on the first try. Okay, I can. But still.
In this corner, your quads! In the other corner, the hack squat! Place your bets!
Strength isn't always loud. Sometimes it is the quiet choice to show up again tomorrow.
Plyo push-ups are just push-ups that got scared and jumped.
Waking early, stretching, breathing. It isn't glamorous. It's how monks become masters.
Being strong isn't about never getting knocked down. It's about how fast you find your feet again.
Sokka, if you grunt any louder on that row, the whole North Pole is going to answer.
Shoulder health is like a good pot of tea. Tend it gently and it will warm you for years.
(Momo's thoughts) Why is the human lying on the floor with his legs up the wall? Is he hunting bugs? I love bugs.
Bosco and I did walking lunges around the palace today. Bosco won. Bosco is a bear.
Everything is connected. How you sleep, eat and breathe shows up in how you pull.
(Says nothing. Does forty clap push-ups. Leaves.)
My glider taught me the wind does most of the work if you're set up right. So does good mobility.
I spent years behind walls believing I was safe. True safety is knowing you can stand on your own.
Hakoda once rowed a canoe for three days straight, then complained his biceps weren't pumped enough.
The fire does not fear the water. It simply knows when to rest.
Active recovery is just regular exercise that's trying to be polite.
I'm not saying sand sprints are hard, but my ancestors just filed a complaint.
Healing is training too. Caring for your shoulders today keeps you on the court tomorrow.
I was banished for three years and I still came back for chest day. That's commitment.
A light heart travels far. Carry less resentment and your legs will carry you farther.
Even a small stone, thrown with intent, can change the course of a river.
Hammer curls? I don't even own a hammer. I own a boomerang and a dream.
I used to think strength meant never asking for help. Asking is what made me stronger.
Remember, Aang: if a sky bison sits on your foam roller, it is now the sky bison's foam roller.
The Boulder is conflicted. The Boulder wants to squat. The Boulder also wants a nap.
Prepare for the storm while the sea is calm. That is what posture work is for.
And now, a dramatic reenactment of your final set! (The actor collapses. The crowd weeps.)
One step at a time is still flying, as long as you keep taking them.
The best stance is the one you can hold when life pushes back. Practice it on the easy days.
The swamp spirits say do one more set. Or that's just the swamp gas. Hard to tell.
Style is just the shape your discipline takes. Keep showing up and your style will find you.
Drink this onion and banana juice. It will open your chakras. It will also open your eyes. Very wide.
Deadlifts are just earthbending with extra steps and a lot more grunting. Love it.
Hope is something you carry. Pack it with you every morning, like fresh water.
If your shoulder blades won't squeeze together, I could chi-block them together! Kidding. Mostly.
Sleep is the cheapest and most powerful potion in all four nations.
Earthbending is staying steady when everything else isn't. So is life. So is the fourth set.
Face pulls are great for your shoulders and terrible for your dignity.
Explosive power comes from a calm center. The quieter the mind, the faster the hands.
A day without training is simply a day with more time for tea. I see no problem here.
My cabbages are more stable than your single-leg RDL, and they don't even have legs!
A waterbender who rushes spills. Slow the lowering and keep everything in the cup.
Lightning can be redirected. Sadly, so can a bench press that wasn't racked properly.
Your body keeps every promise you make it. Make it gentle promises today.
A strong foundation forgives a hundred mistakes built on top of it.
I am literally the moon, and even I can see that pull-up wasn't full range.
Friendship and strength are built the same way: by showing up for years.
Hip mobility is crucial for volleyball. And for running away from Fire Nation ships.
There are no sore legs in Ba Sing Se. Here, we all walk down stairs very comfortably.
The river does not fight the rock. It goes around, over and through, and it always arrives.
Master Piandao says I have potential. He was looking at my triceps. I think.
Air Nomads travel in circles. Every return makes the circle a little wider.
Do not envy the oak. It was once an acorn that simply held its ground.
Sokka tried to waterbend his dumbbells. They did not move. Neither did his ego.
My uncle told me to look inward. The strongest press starts with a stable core.
Monk Tashi once meditated so long he forgot his own name. That's dedication. Or a really good nap.
Calf raises? I've been raising calves my whole life. It's a tundra joke. Nobody laughs.
You don't have to be the strongest. You have to be the one who doesn't give up.
I threw a hundred knives today. My rotator cuff would like to file a formal complaint.
One calm breath before the serve is worth more than a thousand clenched teeth.
Speed is useless if your footing is weak. Earn your quickness from the ground up.
Your rows are sloppy. Like a penguin trying to sled uphill.
Fire is life, not destruction. Let your training warm you, not burn you down.
Rest day? Fine. But if anyone touches my foam roller, they're getting a rock to the shin.
Box jumps! I love a good box. I love a good jump. Put them together? GENIUS!
The ocean is patient with the shore. Be that patient with your progress.
Ugh! Why is the dip station always taken by someone just standing on it?!
Peace is not something you wait for. It is a practice, like any other stance.
Listen with your feet. The sand tells you where to go before the ball does.
Hydration tip from a Water Tribe warrior: drink water. That's it. I'm a genius.
When frustration flares, pour that fire into the next rep, not into yourself.
(Momo's thoughts) The human does box breathing. I do box sitting. Inside the box. Very relaxing.
My secret to explosive legs? Pure stubbornness. And squats. Okay, mostly squats.
Under the swamp, all the roots are one tree. Your grip, your back and your swing are one, too.
Nyla and I have a rule: nobody leaves until their arms shake like a shirshu's whiskers.
Flexibility isn't only for your hamstrings. Bend your plans and you won't break.
The secret to great power is knowing when to wait. Wait... wait... then move like an avalanche.
Sokka keeps asking me to spot his curls. Son, nobody spots curls.
The master is not the one who never misses. The master is the one who resets and tries again.
My mobility routine: stretch, think about meat, stretch, think about meat again.
The Boulder respects the trap bar. The trap bar does not respect the Boulder's lower back.
Leading isn't shouting orders. It's being the first one on the boat, every single day.
The Fire Nation has many great inventions. Pre-workout tea is my personal favorite.
Let the stretch arrive on its own. You cannot pull a flower open.
Don't measure yourself against the mountain. Measure yourself against yesterday's pebble.
I rowed my cabbage boat across the whole bay and still had the arms to shake my fist at the Avatar!
Balance your push with your pull, and your fire will burn for a lifetime.
Appa wants you to know the beach walk is mandatory. Appa also wants six hundred pounds of hay.
I don't do cardio. I do chasing my runaway cabbage cart down a mountain. Same thing.
Mastery is not a destination. It is a promise you renew with every repetition.
My overhead press strategy: look determined, breathe loudly, and hope my arms catch up.
The leaf does not argue with the wind. It dances, and arrives exactly where it should.
I grew tall by treating every single day as if it mattered. It always did.
Grip training is important. You never know when you'll need to hang off a flying bison for an hour.
Fine. I'll admit it. The external rotations were worth it. Do not tell Uncle I said that.
One hundred sixty-four days. Every element, every breath. You didn't just train. You became someone new.

loading: Brewing a pot of jasmine tea…
Sokka is drawing the map. It has a lot of arrows.
Appa is shedding on the scrolls again. One moment…
Unrolling the scroll the right way up…
Toph is feeling the vibrations of your progress…
Calibrating the Avatar State. Please do not glow yet.
Momo stole the schedule. Retrieving it…
Asking the Boulder for a spot…

empty.noLogs: No sets logged yet. The scroll is as empty as Sokka's battle plans.
empty.noLogsSub: Log a set on any workout and your best lifts will appear here.
empty.firstTime: First time on this one. No pressure. Okay, a little pressure. That's how adaptation works.
empty.noCompletions: No elements mastered yet. Even Aang started with marbles.
empty.noStreak: Every streak begins with one day. Today looks suspiciously available.
empty.gapText: You pushed this day back, so it's officially tea time. Training resumes on the next scroll.
empty.notes: How did it feel? Jump heights, PRs, cabbage-related incidents…
empty.beforeStart: The training arc begins in {n} days. Hydrate. Sharpen your boomerang.
empty.afterEnd: The arc is complete. You are fully realized. (Season Two not yet announced.)

earth: Toph would call that barely adequate, which from her is a standing ovation.
The Boulder is proud. The Boulder is also tired, and he only watched.
Your legs are now legally classified as boulders.
Somewhere, a badgermole nods in respect.
King Bumi is laughing maniacally in approval.
water: Your back is now wider than the Northern Water Tribe's wall.
Katara says you can stop flexing at your reflection now.
Even the Moon Spirit noticed those pull-ups.
Master Pakku grudgingly admits that was precise.
You flowed like water. Sweaty, sweaty water.
fire: Uncle Iroh has prepared celebratory tea.
Zuko says that was honorable. He's very intense about it.
Your triceps are now officially a fire hazard.
Jeong Jeong approves, but asks that you respect the fire... and stretch.
air: Light as a leaf on the wind.
Monk Gyatso would have baked you a celebratory fruit pie.
Your hips are now 12% more Air Nomad.
Momo stole your water bottle in celebration.

shift: The schedule bends like water. Everything moved forward one day.
Cabbage cart rerouted. The arc now ends {end}.
Even the Avatar spent a century in an iceberg. One day is fine.
undo: Undone. The cabbages have been restored.
Time reversed. Don't tell Wan Shi Tong.
streak: Every streak starts at zero. Even Aang's.
One day down. The journey of a thousand miles, et cetera.
Three in a row! Sokka is drawing you a celebratory map.
A full week. Toph says you're not completely useless.
Two weeks strong. The Boulder is impressed.
Thirty days! You're basically a Kyoshi Warrior now.
Sixty days. Uncle Iroh is writing a proverb about you.
One hundred days. The Order of the White Lotus has taken notice.

io.exported: Scroll saved. Guard it like the Earth King guards Bosco.
io.badFile: That scroll is unreadable. Even Wan Shi Tong couldn't make sense of it.
io.resetConfirm: This erases every check, log and shift on this device. Even the cabbage merchant would hesitate.
io.resetDone: Fresh scroll. The arc begins anew.

notes.quotes: Original lines written in the voice of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters. Fan homage, not affiliated.
